name: Validate and pay external manager fees
summary: About 120 external public market managers bill management fees, and some performance fees, after each quarter. A senior accountant in investment accounting matches each invoice to the mandate's fee schedule, recalculates the fee from custodian asset values, queries the manager when the figures differ, and has it approved before it is paid, mostly by the organisation as agent for its clients and otherwise from pool accounts. Validated fees then clear the monthly accruals and feed cost allocation and net-of-fee returns. The work is slowed by invoices arriving in waves after quarter end, by managers billing on their own asset values, and by approvals that queue at the same time.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion that pays roughly $190 million a year of external fees as agent for four client institutions.
baseline.notes: Fee schedules in agreement PDFs, one fee workbook per manager, custodian valuations, ERP accounts payable and custodian payment portal; no fee validation software.

trigger: An external manager's quarterly (sometimes monthly) fee invoice arrives in the fund accounting mailbox.
end_state: The fee is agreed, approved, paid and recorded in the ledger and cost database; or the invoice is returned as not payable.

volume.seasonality: Most invoices arrive in the four to eight weeks after each calendar quarter end; the month after quarter end can carry two to three times the average.

evidence.note: Organisation file process map (30 to 60, mode 45): about 124 mandates billing quarterly, some aggregated into one invoice, while fees deducted at source need no invoice, as the model manager's cost report footnote distinguishes.
Five senior accountants in the organisation file; about 2.7 hands-on hours per invoice at 45 invoices a month is about 0.95 FTE, within the 3.1 FTE not claimed by other workflows.
About 10 minutes per invoice plus returned items.

roles.title: Senior analyst, manager research and operational due diligence

evidence.note: Cost from the organisation file. About 12% of invoices need fee-term confirmation or performance fee review; within the 0.9 FTE of the role not claimed by other workflows.
Cost from the organisation file; about 4 or 5 approvals a month.
Cost from the organisation file; about 34 agency invoices a month at about 12 minutes each.

roles.title: Manager, financial reporting and corporate accounting

evidence.note: Cost from the organisation file; release of weekly payment runs, share attributable to manager fees.
Cost from the organisation file; about 11 pool-paid invoices a month.

Document management system and virtual data rooms
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)

steps.name: Receive and log the manager's invoice
steps.description: A senior accountant picks the invoice up from the fund accounting mailbox, saves it to the manager's folder and adds it to the fee tracker with manager, billing period, accounts, amount and due date. Most invoices arrive in the four to eight weeks after each quarter end, so they come in waves.

error.defect_description: Billing period or amount typed wrongly in the tracker.

evidence.note: Invoices for investment services arrive weeks after the period; queue time at quarter-end peaks is an author estimate.

steps.name: Match the invoice to the mandate and fee schedule
steps.description: The accountant finds the mandate's management agreement and fee schedule, checks that the legal entity, accounts and billing period on the invoice belong to an active mandate, and notes the fee basis: tiered rates, aggregation with related accounts, minimum fees, any most-favoured-nation discount and the asset values to use.

error.defect_description: An amended fee schedule is overlooked.

next.condition: duplicate or billed for a terminated mandate; returned to the manager

evidence.note: Shares are author estimates; fee schedules sit in the executed manager mandate per the organisation file.

steps.name: Manager research confirms the current fee terms
steps.description: When the schedule was amended, renegotiated or is ambiguous, a manager research analyst who owns the relationship confirms the agreed terms and effective date, often by checking the side letter or emailing the manager.

evidence.note: The model manager renegotiated fees across its roster in 2019 to 2020, so amended schedules were common; effort is an author estimate.

steps.name: Pull market values for the billing period
steps.description: The accountant downloads month-end or daily market values for each account in the mandate from the custodian's accounting records, adjusts for contributions and withdrawals during the quarter as the agreement requires, and converts currencies at the agreed rates.

error.defect_description: Wrong valuation dates or a missed mid-quarter cash flow.

evidence.note: Valuations from an authorised source are a SOC 1 baseline objective; the custodian is the independent value source here.

steps.name: Recalculate the management fee
steps.description: In the manager's fee workbook the accountant applies the rate tiers, aggregation and discounts to the asset values for each month or day of the period and totals the fee by account, then documents the calculation for review.

error.defect_description: Formula or tier error in the fee workbook.

evidence.note: About 8% of invoices with performance fees reflects the alternatives and some active mandates; author's estimate.

steps.name: Recalculate the performance fee
steps.description: For a performance fee the accountant obtains the mandate's return and benchmark return for the measurement period from the performance team's records, applies the hurdle, high-water mark, cap and any clawback in the agreement, and computes the fee owed.

error.defect_description: High-water mark or crystallisation date applied wrongly.

evidence.note: Performance fee mechanics are standard; effort and wait for returns are author estimates.

steps.name: Manager research reviews the performance fee
steps.description: A manager research analyst checks the performance fee calculation against the agreement and the manager's own return figures and confirms the fee is consistent with how the mandate actually performed.

control.basis: Fee validation procedure: performance fees are reviewed by the investment team that oversees the mandate before approval

evidence.note: The organisation file lists manager research among the roles of this process; the review rule is an author assumption.

steps.name: Compare the recalculated fee with the invoice
steps.description: The accountant compares the model manager's figure with the invoice account by account and checks whether any difference is within the tolerance in the fee procedure, usually a small percentage or dollar amount caused by rounding or day counts.

control.basis: Fee validation procedure under the model manager's cost governance: every invoice is independently recalculated and agreed within tolerance before payment

evidence.note: The model manager describes cost governance with tiered approvals; the 22% exception rate is an author estimate (different asset values, cash flow timing, rate tiers).

steps.name: Query the manager on the difference
steps.description: The accountant sends the manager's operations or billing team the model manager's calculation and asks them to explain the difference or reissue the invoice. Common causes are the manager billing on its own valuations, missed mid-quarter flows or an old rate.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the manager's explanation or revised invoice
steps.description: The manager reviews its billing, then either sends a revised invoice or explains its figures, which may show that the model manager's calculation needs correcting. Replies take from a couple of days to several weeks around quarter end.

next.condition: explanation needs new values or terms

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Code the invoice and prepare the approval package
steps.description: The accountant splits the fee by pool or client account and cost category, records the expected accrual it will clear, and attaches the recalculation, the agreement extract and any correspondence for the approver.

error.defect_description: Fee charged to the wrong client account.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Director approves the invoice for payment
steps.description: The director of investment accounting reviews the package, the variance explanation and the account coding and approves the payment within delegated signing authority, or sends it back. Approvals bunch up after quarter end.

control.basis: Delegation of signing authority: the preparer cannot approve, and fees are approved within tiered approval limits

evidence.note: Tiered approval authorities are named in the model manager's cost governance; the threshold share is an author estimate.

steps.name: CFO approves a large fee payment
steps.description: Invoices above the director's limit, such as large performance fees or quarterly fees on the biggest mandates, go to the chief financial officer for a second approval.

control.basis: Delegation of signing authority: payments above the director's limit need CFO approval

evidence.note: Tiered approvals are described; the CFO limit is not public.

steps.name: Prepare the payment instruction
steps.description: For fees the model manager pays as agent the accountant sends the approved invoice and coding to accounts payable; for fees borne by a pool it enters a payment instruction against the pool's custody account. The fee is also flagged to cash management so the account is funded.

error.defect_description: Wrong payee bank details or account selected.

next.condition: paid by the model manager as agent
paid from a pool custody account

evidence.note: The model manager pays most external fees as agent on clients' behalf; the 75/25 split is an author estimate.

steps.name: Accounts payable enters the invoice in the ERP
steps.description: The accounts payable clerk keys the approved invoice into the ERP against the manager's vendor record, checks the approval evidence and bank details on file, and schedules it in the next payment run.

evidence.note: Agency fees are paid to vendors on receipt of billings; the ERP route is an author assumption.

steps.name: Release the payment run
steps.description: Once a week the manager of financial reporting reviews the payment run listing against approvals and releases it in the bank portal as the second authoriser.

control.basis: Dual authorisation of payment runs: the person who enters invoices does not release payments

evidence.note: Weekly payment runs and dual release are common practice; author's estimate.

steps.name: Cash team authorises the payment from the pool account
steps.description: A cash and collateral analyst checks the pool has cash for the value date and authorises the payment instruction in the custodian portal as second signer.

control.basis: Payment authorisation matrix: dual authorisation in the custodian portal, preparer cannot release

evidence.note: Mirrors dual authorisation of custody payments in the organisation's capital call workflow.

steps.name: Bank or custodian sends the payment
steps.description: The bank or custodian executes the wire or electronic funds transfer to the manager on the value date and reports it on the next statement.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm payment and clear the fee accrual
steps.description: The accountant confirms the payment on the bank or custodian statement, books the actual fee against the accrual carried in the pool or client portfolio, and notes any difference from the accrual for month end.

error.defect_description: Accrual not reversed, so the fee is counted twice.

control.basis: Accrual accounting: investment management fees are accrued and trued up to actual invoices (GIPS for asset owners recommendation and month-end close)

next.condition: payment returned or rejected by the bank

evidence.note: GIPS for asset owners recommends accruing investment management fees; return rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Record the validated fee in the investment cost database
steps.description: The accountant adds the final fee by mandate, pool and client portfolio to the investment cost database used for cost allocation, net-of-fee performance and the annual cost benchmarking survey, and closes the tracker line.

error.defect_description: Fee attributed to the wrong mandate.

evidence.note: Net-of-fee returns deduct external fees and the model manager reports external management fees by asset class; batching is an author estimate.

exceptions.name: Invoice differs from the recalculation
exceptions.description: The manager used its own asset values, missed a cash flow or applied an old rate, so the invoice is queried and reissued or the model manager's calculation corrected.

exceptions.name: Fee terms changed or unclear
exceptions.description: Manager research confirms an amended schedule or side letter before the recalculation.

exceptions.name: Performance fee
exceptions.description: The invoice includes a performance fee that is recalculated against hurdle and high-water mark and reviewed by manager research.

exceptions.name: Above the director's limit
exceptions.description: Large invoices need CFO approval as well.

exceptions.name: Duplicate or not payable
exceptions.description: A duplicate invoice or a bill for a terminated mandate is returned to the manager.

exceptions.name: Payment returned
exceptions.description: The bank rejects or returns the payment and a new instruction is prepared.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from invoice receipt to payment confirmed and recorded
benchmarks.population: External manager fee invoices at a Canadian public-sector asset manager, 2019 to 2022

evidence.note: No published benchmark; management agreements commonly allow about 30 days to pay, clean invoices take two to three weeks through recalculation, approval and a weekly payment run, and queried invoices four to eight weeks.
Agency fees paid or payable on behalf of members, note 5.
Includes fees deducted at source and estimated second-layer fees; excludes performance fees.
Shows fees are collected from clients ahead of managers' billings.
Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Managers bill on their own asset values and cash flow timing, so a fifth of invoices need a query and wait weeks for a reply.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the common causes of differences.

pain_points.description: Fee terms sit in agreement PDFs and side letters and are rebuilt in one workbook per manager, so amendments are missed and the knowledge sits with a few people.

evidence.note: Frequent fee renegotiation across the roster in 2019 to 2020.

pain_points.description: Invoices arrive in waves after quarter end, when the same accountants and the director are also closing the quarter, so invoices and approvals queue.

evidence.note: Service invoices arrive up to 60 days after the period, overlapping quarter-end close.

pain_points.description: Two payment routes (agency through the ERP and pool custody accounts) with separate approvals and funding make it easy to lose track of what has been paid and what is still accrued.

evidence.note: The model manager collects agency fees from clients in advance and pays on billing, holding $9.2 million collected but unbilled at end 2021.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: As an agent the model manager administers external management, custodial and other investment fees under contracts held by the clients, collects them from clients and pays vendors on receipt of billings; agency investment management fees paid or payable $190.6 million in 2021 ($184.5 million in 2020); agency fees collected but not yet billed $9.2 million at 31 December 2021; external management fees in the cost report $291.0 million in 2021 ($246.1 million in 2020), covering managers that invoice separately and those that deduct fees at source, excluding performance fees.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: The model manager rationalised its external manager roster, eliminated fund-of-funds structures and used its scale to negotiate fee reductions; cost governance includes tiered approval authorities and actual and forecast expenses monitored against budget.

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: The model manager incurs investment management and custodial fees on the pension client's behalf; private market management fees are deducted from managed assets; the pension client's investment fees and the model manager cost recovery were 0.41% of average net assets in 2021.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Fee calculation and billing is listed among SOC 1 areas to consider; baseline objectives cover valuation from authorised sources and reconciliation.

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Net-of-fees total fund returns must deduct investment management fees for externally managed segregated accounts; asset owners should accrue investment management fees and costs.

sources.title: Custody Bank RFP, Appendix F: Performance Standards and Related Key Performance Indicators
sources.supports: A public pension fund requires its custodian's service invoices no later than 60 days after the prior period end, showing that investment service invoices commonly arrive weeks after the period they cover.

sources.title: Wages: Accountant (NOC 11100), Toronto region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages low 25.00, median 41.34, high 74.36 (2023-2024), the base of the organisation file's accountant costs.

sources.title: Wages: Finance Director (NOC 10010), Toronto region

assumptions: One case is one invoice, which may cover several accounts of one manager. Fees that external funds deduct at source, and private fund management fees called through capital calls, are not invoiced and are not part of this process.

The organisation file lists the external manager mandate from ext-manager-onboarding as a trigger; it is placed in interfaces.inputs because the fee schedule is a standing input and does not start a case.

About 75% of invoices are paid by the model manager as agent through its own accounts payable after collecting the fees from clients, and 25% are paid from pool custody accounts for managers of pooled strategies; the split is an author estimate based on the model manager's agency fee note and the four pools operating in 2021.
Monthly fee accruals are booked in fund-accounting-close; this process only clears them against the actual invoice.
Roles outside the process map (CFO, accounts payable clerk, manager of financial reporting, cash and collateral analyst) are organisation file roles that approve or release payments.

Times and probabilities are author estimates (tier C) unless a source is cited; no published time study of institutional fee validation was found, and web search capacity ran out while researching this file.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading).
